The core insight is that positional flexibility acts as a buffer against injury-induced performance degradation. The authors model this using two key components: (1) a logistic regression estimating injury likelihood as a function of player age, and (2) a robust optimization framework simulating worst-case injury scenarios. The former enables GSI to predict injury risk dynamically, while the latter allows GSE to compute optimal player-position assignments under uncertainty. Platoon advantages are embedded within the flexibility framework, enhancing its predictive power. The value of flexibility emerges as a scalar measure of expected run contribution above replacement, derived from comparing performance outcomes with and without flexible rosters. Failure modes include misalignment between predicted and actual injury durations, or over-reliance on static platoon strategies.
